stories.title: Michigan’s Arab American News publisher sues Mike Rogers, campaign over alleged defamation
stories.summary: The publisher of Michigan's Arab American News, Osama Siblani, has filed a defamation lawsuit in Wayne County Circuit Court against former U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers and his campaign. The suit alleges false statements were made about Siblani, including claims he called for American Jews to 'return to Poland' and justified Hamas attacks. Rogers' campaign maintains the statements were true.

stories.title: An herbicide had a strange effect on this weed. What we're still learning about dicamba's impact
stories.summary: University of Michigan research indicates that low doses of the herbicide dicamba, which can drift miles from application sites, cause wood sorrel weeds to produce more, but smaller, flowers. This hormetic response could alter surrounding ecosystems and pollinator interactions, though the study did not find the weed became stronger over generations.

stories.title: Plymouth testing cameras at train crossing. Here's where and why
stories.summary: Plymouth, Michigan, is launching a one-year pilot program to help motorists avoid train delays at the North Main Street railroad crossing. Solar-powered cameras will monitor the crossing, allowing drivers to check for blockages via a website or app. The program costs the city $3,500, with potential for expansion.

stories.title: Southern Michigan communities turn to regional management of growing deer herds
stories.summary: Southern Michigan communities are increasingly adopting regional approaches to manage growing deer populations, aiming to reduce car crashes, protect biodiversity, and keep deer out of neighborhoods. Coalitions in Kent County and a group including Farmington Hills, Farmington, and Southfield are implementing strategies like roadside mowing, increased hunting permits, and professional sharpshooters, with some programs donating venison to food banks.

stories.title: Canton woman gets 16 insurance notices for treatments she never had; provider found billing under her name
stories.summary: A Canton woman received 16 insurance notices for medical treatments she never had, including cancer care. After media intervention, UnitedHealthcare stated a Florida provider billed the claims in her name. The insurer denied the claims, confirming she has no financial responsibility, and explained that benefit statements are issued even for denied claims.

stories.title: Priced out: Why Ann Arbor housing keeps getting more expensive, and what the city is doing about it
stories.summary: Ann Arbor's housing costs are significantly higher than national averages, with median home prices rising nearly 50% since 2016 to $618,838. The city's Comprehensive Land Use Plan, approved in March 2026, aims to address this by opening up single-family areas to low-rise residential developments, despite some community concerns about gentrification and green spaces.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor AFSCME employees ratify new contract with the city
inputFacts.summary: Members of AFSCME Local 369 have voted to ratify a new three-year contract with the City of Ann Arbor by a 97.5% margin. The agreement includes the largest wage increase for city employees since the early 1990s and now awaits final approval from the City Council.

inputFacts.title: Why Detroit cowboy brought his horse on a bus: ‘I’m everywhere with my horses’
inputFacts.summary: Detroit cowboy Jordan Williams staged a viral stunt by bringing his horse onto a city bus to raise awareness for his Urban City Cowboys organization, which provides equestrian therapy and rodeo lessons. While the city acknowledged the positive intent behind the stunt, officials noted it raised safety concerns and announced that bus operators will undergo retraining on transit policies.

inputFacts.title: Detroit Land Bank property on city’s east side draws complaints over trash, unsafe conditions
inputFacts.summary: Neighbors are reporting ongoing issues with a vacant Detroit Land Bank property on Lappin, citing trash, squatters, and property damage. While cleanup efforts have begun, the city is currently reviewing the structure for potential demolition.

inputFacts.title: Girl stabbed multiple times at gas station on Detroit’s east side
inputFacts.summary: A young girl was hospitalized in critical condition after being stabbed multiple times at a gas station on Detroit's east side on Friday evening. Police detained a suspect at the scene and are currently investigating the incident.

inputFacts.title: An anti-Muslim flyer targeted a Taylor restaurant. The community responds with an outpouring of support.
inputFacts.summary: A Taylor restaurant, Halal Bros 2 Go, received an outpouring of community support and increased sales after an anti-Muslim flyer targeting the business was distributed at a nearby mall. The owner, Khaled Algomai, has invited those with questions about his business or halal practices to visit the restaurant for a conversation.

inputFacts.title: Detroit school board candidate raises over $75,500 in 2026 election
inputFacts.summary: Detroit school board candidate Dr. Jameel Smith has raised over $75,500 for the 2026 election, significantly outpacing other candidates in campaign funding. Smith utilized these funds to hire professional campaign staff and consultants, while other candidates reported minimal or no expenditures for traditional advertising.

inputFacts.title: El-Sayed backs Maryland’s Chris Van Hollen as US Senate majority leader battle begins
inputFacts.summary: Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has endorsed Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen in his challenge against Chuck Schumer for the U.S. Senate majority leader position. The move follows the Democratic party's recent success in the November 3 election, with El-Sayed calling for new leadership to better represent working families.
